title: Define foreign exchange as FEMA, 1999 does, and describe how the foreign exchange market is organised and who takes part in it
Read exchange rate quotations: direct and indirect quotes, two-way (bid and offer) quotes, and cash, tom, spot and forward value dates
Work out customer (merchant) rates, forward rates and cross rates from interbank quotes
Explain the factors that determine exchange rates and how the exchange rate mechanism works
Describe how a bank's foreign exchange dealing room operates and is controlled
Identify the derivative products used in foreign exchange business and what each is used for
Apply the RBI and FEDAI guidelines that govern foreign exchange dealings
Explain what correspondent banking is, why banks need it, and which services depend on an account relationship
Distinguish Nostro, Vostro, Loro and mirror accounts from the direction of the relationship, and reconcile a Nostro balance
Describe the electronic modes of transmission and payment systems used for cross-border and domestic funds transfer: SWIFT, CHIPS, Fedwire, CHAPS, TARGET, RTGS and NEFT
Identify who is an NRI or PIO under FEMA and distinguish NRE, NRO, FCNR(B) and SNRR accounts by purpose, currency, deposit form, credits, debits and repatriability
Apply the conditions for advances against non-resident deposits and for housing loans to NRIs
Describe the facilities available to NRIs for investing in India: shares and securities, funds, deposits, firms and immovable property
Distinguish capital account and current account transactions and explain how the Foreign Exchange Management Act treats each
Apply the Liberalised Remittance Scheme: who is eligible, the annual limit, frequency, documents and how family and proprietors are treated
Identify the remittances that are permitted and those that are prohibited under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
Apply the operational conditions for capital account remittances and for gifts and loans to non-resident relatives under the scheme
Work out tax collected at source on remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
State the reporting and other remittance facilities for residents that accompany the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
Define a documentary letter of credit and identify each party to it and what it does
Distinguish the types of letter of credit: irrevocable, confirmed, transferable, red and green clause, sight, usance, deferred payment, negotiation, back-to-back, standby and revolving
Trace the flow of an export letter of credit and an import letter of credit from application to payment
Apply the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) and the liabilities, responsibilities and rights of the parties
Scrutinise documents under a credit, handle discrepancies, crystallise import bills and follow up bills
Identify the risks in letter of credit transactions and the safeguards available to banks
Explain standby letters of credit and how they compare with guarantees
Apply the Uniform Rules for Bank-to-Bank Reimbursements (URR 725)
Apply International Standard Banking Practice (ISBP 745) when examining documents
Apply the Incoterms 2020 rules to allocate cost, risk and delivery between buyer and seller
